# ChatCode CLI Chat Import **A ChatCode CLI plugin that imports conversation history from 19 AI coding tools, so you can continue right where you left off.** > **All sessions, continued in ChatCode CLI.** [![English](https://img.shields.io/badge/lang-English-blue.svg)](README.md) [![简体中文](https://img.shields.io/badge/lang-%E7%AE%80%E4%BD%93%E4%B8%AD%E6%96%87-red.svg)](README.zh-CN.md) [![version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@chatcode/cco-chat-import?style=flat&label=version&color=4D6BFE)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@chatcode/cco-chat-import) [![downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/@chatcode/cco-chat-import?style=flat&label=downloads&color=4D6BFE)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@chatcode/cco-chat-import) [![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/Nwflower/dsh-chat-import?style=flat&label=%E2%98%85&color=08C)](https://github.com/Nwflower/dsh-chat-import) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-2EA44F?style=flat)](LICENSE)
## Intro `ChatCode CLI Chat Import` imports conversation history with full context from other agents, turning it into a seamlessly resumable ChatCode CLI session. Now covers import from 19 agents: Claude Code, Codex, ChatGPT, Cursor, Gemini, Reasonix, opencode, MiMo Code, ZCode, Grok Build, OpenClaw, Pi Coding Agent, Hermes, Kimi CLI / Kimi Code, Qoder CLI, WorkBuddy, Qwen Work CN (千问办公), and legacy DSH session logs. Export back to: Claude Code, Codex, Kimi Code. ## Install ```bash chatcode-cli plugin --profile web add @chatcode/cco-chat-import # npm package chatcode-cli plugin --profile web add -w link:/path/to/cco-chat-import # local checkout (symlink) ``` ## Usage ### Startup auto import On the first ChatCode CLI startup after installing the plugin, existing ChatCode CLI history is scanned and imported automatically. The lower-left sidebar shows the scan state, then `completed / total` while importing, followed by the total, successful, failed, and skipped counts for five seconds. Later startups do not rescan when `imports.json` already exists. 1. **Import** — pick the conversations to import from the "Import sessions" panel in the bottom-right of the GUI and import with one click, or have your agent call the context tool: ``` import_chat({ format: "claude", path: "~/.claude/projects" }) import_chat({ format: "chatgpt", path: "~/Downloads/chatgpt-export/conversations.json" }) import_chat({ format: "local-jsonl", path: "D:\downloads\session.jsonl" }) ``` Reasonix directory imports conservatively collapse only recovery ancestors proven by both a strict semantic prefix and an explicit `parent_id` lineage. Ambiguous or divergent files remain separate; use `lineageMode: "physical"` for one session per JSONL. Claude Code imports exclude complete, known CLI-injected tag-wrapped records (such as command context and system reminders) from user turns. External-agent transcripts carry a **protected empty `system/message` head** as the first surface message (inside the first step, before any user turn). The source transcript has no real system prompt, so the head is intentionally empty — it reserves the required head slot so that re-opening an imported session after a restart can legally inject the engine's system prompt on resume, instead of a corrupt mid-log `system/message`. Native ChatCode CLI / DSH logs retain their existing system head, developer messages, and compaction history. Surface replacement ranges and event references are remapped together when runtime events are removed, so compressed histories remain resumable. If an earlier native import fails to resume, re-import the original file with `import_chat` using `format: "cco", force: true` to create a fresh copy. Existing stored logs are not rewritten. 2. **Resume** — refresh the session list, open the imported session, and keep chatting from where the source left off. 3. **Sync (optional)** — the panel's "Sync" tab offers bidirectional incremental sync, off by default. Sub-agent conversations are filtered out by default in both directions. Full tool / command usage (parameters, examples, edge cases) lives in **[docs/USAGE.md](docs/USAGE.md)**. ## Hooks, MCP and commands The plugin bundle includes an assets plugin, so CLI and Web users do not need to add hook or MCP entries to `cordis.patch.yml`. On every startup it reads the selected `$CHATCODE_CLI_HOME` (legacy `$DSH_HOME`, default `~/.chatcode-cli`), creates `settings.json` with an empty `hooks` object only when the file is missing, and mounts the native Claude command-hook bridge. Existing settings are preserved. Project `.chatcode-cli/settings.json` and `settings.local.json` hooks are also loaded. Hook bridge and MCP client packages are supplied by ChatCode CLI; another host must provide compatible peers. MCP reads both user and current-project configuration. Precedence is the current project's `.mcp.json`, then project `.chatcode-cli/settings.local.json`, `settings.json` and `.mcp.json`, then ancestor `.mcp.json` files, followed by `~/.chatcode-cli.json` and the selected home's `.mcp.json` and `settings.json`. Different names are combined; each duplicate name uses its highest-priority declaration. `/hooks` and `/mcp-status` inspect the current session's project and show source paths. Servers marked `disabled: true` are skipped. `${VAR}` and `{env:VAR}` references are resolved from the startup environment. Explicit hook paths and MCP server names in the user's plugin tree take precedence, including disabled entries, so existing manual and migrated configuration is not mounted twice. The host filesystem provider reads user and project `commands/*.md` directly for `/name` invocation, and reads skills from their own directories. Commands remain in `commands`; startup and invocation never generate a skill copy or `.chatcode-command.json`. The provider re-reads the command body on invocation and watches command additions, changes and deletions. Within one scope a same-name skill takes precedence; project commands override user commands. This requires a ChatCode CLI host with direct Markdown command support. Legacy `auto-movein.done` markers do not suppress startup asset loading. Restart after editing hooks or MCP. `CHATCODE_CLI_IMPORT_AUTO_MOVEIN=0` disables startup asset loading. Startup removes unedited command skill copies from older releases when their legacy metadata verifies the content, and removes the old metadata. User-edited skills and other files are preserved; records for other projects in the old user-level `cco-chat-import/command-skills.json` remain until those projects are opened. No new command state is created. Explicit ChatCode CLI asset migration also keeps Markdown commands in `commands`; external-agent migration retains its format converters. For an explicit preview or migration from another supported agent, use `import_assets` (default preview, `apply: true` to write) or `cco-chat-import movein`. These tools retain the configuration migration workflow, including permission bridge installation; startup loading uses an already available permission bridge and reports a missing one without downloading packages. ## Features | Capability | Entry points | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | Batch import | `import_chat` (19 formats) · `scan_discover` · sidebar panel | Import 18+ sources with one tool; each conversation becomes its own session | | Import history & purge | sidebar panel **History** tab | View `imports.json` records; remove plugin-created sessions (with confirmation) | | Full-fidelity resume | Imported sessions | Tool calls & results, reasoning, titles, models and timestamps carry over | | Export back | `export_chat` (`format: claude` / `codex` / `kimi`) | Serialize ChatCode CLI sessions back to Claude / Codex / Kimi | | Bidirectional sync | panel "Sync" tab | Incremental sync in both directions (external ↔ ChatCode CLI), off by default | ## Publishing Publishing runs the test suite and a package dry run, including the build checks. Git checks are handled by pnpm for `pnpm publish`; use `pnpm publish --no-git-checks --tag latest --access public --registry https://registry.npmjs.org/` to explicitly allow uncommitted changes. Direct `npm publish` still requires tracked files to be committed and reports a clear error otherwise. ## Docs | Document | Description | | --- | --- | | [Usage Reference](docs/USAGE.md) | Full parameters, examples and edge cases for every tool / command | | [Interchange protocol](docs/INTERCHANGE.md) | Interchange v1 protocol and bundle format | | [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) | Version history | | [Roadmap](ROADMAP.md) | Shipped / planned | | [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) | Development setup, commit rules, security & privacy | ## Star History [![Star History Chart](https://api.star-history.com/chart?repos=Nwflower/dsh-chat-import&type=date&legend=top-left&sealed_token=sAq09Z4DmwD843pzhg7azZtfXs8zW_Xij3fvCo3Ns1BGAgNeP_Zl1xU9YiUacS74_EzDXKHFpW3Bfj13ClcEMRzAhh4mVrl4a20ijURAGU_Oz6RROQYDYw)](https://www.star-history.com/?type=date&repos=Nwflower%2Fdsh-chat-import) Hooks also support user or project `.chatcode-cli/hooks/settings.json` with a top-level `hooks` field, alongside existing settings hooks. Source development requires local plugin sources; `pnpm cco` in registry mode continues to use published plugins. Before packing or publishing, `prepack` rebuilds from source, then packs and extracts the npm artifact to verify user/project hooks and MCP discovery. Source tests do not replace artifact verification. Run `npm run verify:packed-assets` to check the current build. Publish new plugin versions containing these changes, then update both canonical and alias dependencies in the CLI and rebuild it.

# ChatCode CLI Chat Import **ChatCode CLI 会话导入插件，一键导入外部 Agents 的聊天历史并在 ChatCode CLI 中继续对话。** > **所有会话，尽续于此。** [![English](https://img.shields.io/badge/lang-English-blue.svg)](README.md) [![简体中文](https://img.shields.io/badge/lang-%E7%AE%80%E4%BD%93%E4%B8%AD%E6%96%87-red.svg)](README.zh-CN.md) [![version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@chatcode/cco-chat-import?style=flat&label=version&color=4D6BFE)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@chatcode/cco-chat-import) [![downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/@chatcode/cco-chat-import?style=flat&label=downloads&color=4D6BFE)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@chatcode/cco-chat-import) [![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/Nwflower/dsh-chat-import?style=flat&label=%E2%98%85&color=08C)](https://github.com/Nwflower/dsh-chat-import) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-2EA44F?style=flat)](LICENSE)
## 简介 `ChatCode CLI Chat Import` 从其他 Agents 导入含完整上下文的聊天历史，成为可无缝继续的 ChatCode CLI 会话。 现已覆盖 19 种 Agents 的导入：Claude Code、Codex、ChatGPT、Cursor、Gemini、Reasonix、opencode、MiMo Code、ZCode、Grok Build、OpenClaw、Pi Coding Agent、Hermes、Kimi CLI / Kimi Code、Qoder CLI、WorkBuddy、千问办公（Qwen Work CN）与旧版 DSH 会话日志； 下述工具的反向导入：Claude Code、Codex、Kimi Code。 ## 安装 ```bash chatcode-cli plugin --profile web add @chatcode/cco-chat-import # npm 包 chatcode-cli plugin --profile web add -w link:/path/to/cco-chat-import # 本地源码（符号链接） ``` ## 使用 ### 启动自动导入 首次安装后启动 ChatCode CLI 时，插件会自动扫描并导入既有 ChatCode CLI 历史会话。界面左下角会依次显示扫描状态、导入中的「已完成 / 共多少会话」，以及完成后的总数、成功数、失败数和跳过数；完成通知会在 5 秒后关闭。`imports.json` 已存在时，后续启动不会再次扫描。 1. **导入** — 在GUI界面右下角的导入会话面板选择你想导入的会话并一键导入。或让你的Agent调用上下文工具进行导入： ``` import_chat({ format: "claude", path: "~/.claude/projects" }) import_chat({ format: "chatgpt", path: "~/Downloads/chatgpt-export/conversations.json" }) import_chat({ format: "local-jsonl", path: "D:\downloads\session.jsonl" }) ``` Reasonix 目录导入只会折叠同时满足“严格语义前缀”和明确 `parent_id` 谱系证明的恢复祖先。无法证明或真实分叉的文件继续独立保留；`lineageMode: "physical"` 可恢复每个 JSONL 一条会话。 Claude Code 导入会排除完整、已知的 CLI 标签包裹注入记录（例如命令上下文和系统提醒），不将其视为用户提问。 外部 Agent 历史导入后，会在首个有效 step 内、任何用户提问之前，写入一个**受保护的空 `system/message` 首节点**。源 transcript 并无真实系统提示词，故该节点刻意置空——它只是占住所需的首节点槽位，使导入会话在**重启后再次恢复**时，引擎能按合法路径在续聊时注入系统提示词，而不是往历史中部塞入导致损坏的 `system/message`。 原生 ChatCode CLI / DSH 日志保留已有的系统首节点、开发者消息和压缩历史。移除运行时事件时，消息替换范围和事件引用会一起重映射，保证包含历史压缩的会话仍可恢复。 如果先前导入的原生会话无法恢复，请用 `import_chat` 设置 `format: "cco", force: true` 重新导入原文件，生成新的完整副本。已经落盘的日志不会被改写。 2. **续聊** — 刷新会话列表，打开导入的会话，从源记录停下的地方继续对话。 3. **同步（可选）** — 面板「同步」页提供双向增量同步，默认关闭。子代理对话默认双向过滤。 完整工具 / 命令用法（参数、示例、边界行为）见 **[docs/USAGE.zh-CN.md](docs/USAGE.zh-CN.md)**。 ## Hooks、MCP 和 commands 插件组合包已包含资产加载插件，CLI 和 Web 用户无需在 `cordis.patch.yml` 中手动添加 hooks 或 MCP 条目。每次启动都会读取选定的 `$CHATCODE_CLI_HOME`（兼容 `$DSH_HOME`，默认为 `~/.chatcode-cli`）；仅在文件不存在时创建含空 `hooks` 对象的 `settings.json`，并挂载原生 Claude command-hook 桥接。已有设置保持不变。项目 `.chatcode-cli/settings.json` 与 `settings.local.json` 中的 hooks 也会加载。hooks 桥接与 MCP 客户端由 ChatCode CLI 提供；在其他宿主中使用时需提供兼容的 peer 包。 MCP 同时读取用户目录和当前项目：当前项目 `.mcp.json` 优先，其后依次是项目 `.chatcode-cli/settings.local.json`、`settings.json`、`.mcp.json`，再读取祖先目录 `.mcp.json`，最后读取用户的 `~/.chatcode-cli.json`、选定用户目录的 `.mcp.json` 与 `settings.json`。同名服务器只加载优先级最高的一项；不同名称合并加载。`/hooks` 和 `/mcp-status` 也按当前会话的项目目录检查并显示配置来源。跳过 `disabled: true` 的服务器；`${VAR}` 和 `{env:VAR}` 引用从启动环境解析。用户插件树中显式声明的 hook 路径和 MCP 服务器名称优先，包括已禁用的条目，避免与手写或迁移配置重复挂载。 宿主文件系统加载器直接读取用户级和项目级 `commands/*.md`，通过 `/命令名` 调用；skills 从各自的目录读取。命令文件始终保留在 `commands`，启动和调用都不会生成 skill 副本或 `.chatcode-command.json`。调用时重新读取命令正文，命令新增、修改、删除由目录监听刷新。同一作用域内同名 skill 优先，项目命令优先于用户命令。宿主 ChatCode CLI 需支持直接加载 Markdown commands。旧的 `auto-movein.done` 标记不再阻止启动资产加载。修改 hooks、MCP 后重启；`CHATCODE_CLI_IMPORT_AUTO_MOVEIN=0` 可关闭启动资产加载。 启动时根据旧元数据校验内容，仅清理旧版生成且未被修改的命令 skill 副本，并移除旧元数据。手工修改过的 skill 和其他文件会保留；用户级旧 `cco-chat-import/command-skills.json` 中其他项目的记录，在打开对应项目时清理，不再创建新的命令状态。显式迁移 ChatCode CLI 资产也将 Markdown 命令保留在 `commands`；其他 agent 的迁移继续使用各自的格式转换器。 需要显式预览或从其他受支持 agent 迁移时，使用 `import_assets`（默认预览，`apply: true` 落盘）或 `cco-chat-import movein`。这些工具保留配置迁移流程，包括权限桥接安装；启动加载仅使用已经可用的权限桥接，缺失时记录错误，不自动下载包。 ## The format follows [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and
the project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

Release dates are the npm publish timestamps in Asia/Shanghai (UTC+8). Every

# Contributing to dsh-chat-import

Thanks for considering a contribution! `dsh-chat-import` imports external agent
conversation histories into ChatCode CLI as full-fidelity, resumable
sessions. The user-facing contract lives in [README.md](README.md) (bilingual),
and the repo's engineering rules — layout, commit discipline, preserved DSH plugin ABI
constraints, quality conventions — live in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md).

## Dev setup

- **Node.js >= 22.13** (first release where `node:sqlite` is available without a flag)
- `npm ci` — install dependencies (zero runtime deps; peers auto-installed)
- `npm test` — the `node:test` suite (converter unit + export unit + host mock integration)
- `npm run test:live` — run `movein-doctor-live` separately; it spawns real child processes and is timing-sensitive under parallel load, so it is deliberately excluded from `npm test`
- `npm run check:linux` — cross-platform path-discipline guard (enforced in CI)
- `npm run lint` — eslint (flat config)
- `npm run build` — publish-surface self-check (files whitelist + syntax + lockfile version)

## What counts as a change

- **Behavior changes stay honest**: README.md and README.zh-CN.md must stay in
  sync (CI compares heading structure), tests describe the behavior, and any
  file newly referenced by `index.mjs` or the READMEs must join the `files`
  whitelist in `package.json`.
- **Plugin, not engine**: new behavior goes through public dsh host services
  (`sessionPersistence` / `fs` / `tools` / `workspaceRegistry`, optional
  `webServer` / `commands`). Never modify the dsh engine, apiproxy, or official
  UI packages.
- **Imported session logs are append-only and deep-frozen**: never rewrite
  history events; surface events carry `surfaceOp: 'append'`.
- **Fail loudly**: malformed lines and suspected secrets are counted and
  reported, never silently swallowed.

## Commits & PRs

- Conventional commits (`feat:` / `fix:` / `refactor:` / `chore:` / `docs:` /
  `test:`), one logical change per commit; existing history uses Chinese
  descriptions.
- Before pushing: `npm test` + `npm run check:linux` green, working tree clean
  (no `dev/`, `node_modules/` or snapshots staged), `git diff --cached --check`
  clean.
- Fork → `feature/<name>` branch → open a PR (template included). The repo
  pushes straight to `main`; please don't rewrite published history.
- PRs are welcome for new import sources, fidelity upgrades, and the items on
  [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md).

## Security & privacy

Never commit credentials, real user transcripts, or anything under `dev/` (the
local engineering surface, gitignored). In issues and PRs, use **synthetic**
fixtures — no real conversation content.

    "createdAt": 1710000000000,        // 毫秒

  "model": "claude-opus-4-7",           // 源模型（可选）
  "turns": [
    {
      "prompt": "用户提问",
      "steps": [
        {
          "content": [
            { "type": "text", "text": "助手正文" },
            { "type": "reasoning", "text": "推理" },
            { "type": "tool-call", "id": "call-1", "name": "read", "arguments": "{\"path\":\"a\"}" }
          ],
          "toolCalls": [
            { "id": "call-1", "name": "read", "arguments": "{\"path\":\"a\"}" }

# Usage Reference > Full per-tool / per-command usage moved out of the README. See the README "Usage" section for a quick start. ## 🛠 Usage `/import cco ` accepts Web ZIP exports, TUI JSONL, and native-log directories. ZIP archives need no manual extraction: root and child logs become independent sessions, and missing or corrupt attachments fail explicitly. `import_chat({ format: "cco", path, preview: true })` previews without creating sessions or saving attachments. The older `dsh` argument remains an alias. For a TUI session, `/export` (or `/export jsonl`) writes a native JSONL log. Use `/import cco ` to import it, then `/resume` to open the imported session. Directory imports also collect TUI JSONL exports and `session.vN.jsonl` logs. The importer creates an independent root session with the required format and lineage metadata. `/export markdown` is for reading; `.md` files cannot be imported as native logs. Attachment files and child sessions are not bundled in JSONL. > **First-migration step flow** (these steps cover conversation history; see the [README](../README.md#hooks-mcp-and-commands) for startup loading of hooks, MCP and commands): > ① **Preview** - `scan_discover()` or the sidebar panel to inspect importable sessions and status badges; or pass `preview: true` to any `import_*` for a zero-side-effect dry run. > ② **Import** - drop `preview` and import for real; verify the per-session `status` by source / workspace (duplicate-import behavior under "Incremental re-import" below). > ③ **Health check & retract** - `doctor()` read-only check; `retract_import` to remove the registry record, or the panel History tab to delete plugin-created sessions (with confirmation). > **Note:** imports persist to disk immediately, but the ChatCode CLI session list does not auto-refresh — refresh the page (or the session list) after importing to see the new sessions. **Import — a single file or a directory.** Every `import_*` tool takes a `path`; directories are scanned recursively and each file / conversation becomes its own session: ``` import_claude({ path: "C:\Users\\.claude\projects\\.jsonl" }) import_codex({ path: "C:\Users\\.codex\sessions\2026\05\18\rollout-2026-05-18T21-14-16-xxxx.jsonl" }) import_chatgpt({ path: "C:\Users\\Downloads\chatgpt-export\conversations.json" }) import_opencode({ path: "C:\Users\\.local\share\opencode\opencode.db" }) import_local_jsonl({ path: "D:\downloads\session.jsonl" }) ``` `import_local_jsonl({ path })` accepts any local `.jsonl` session file (or directory): it auto-detects `dsh` / `claude` / `codex` / `cursor` / `reasonix` / `pi` / `openclaw` / `hermes`, and the `format` parameter forces one parser when detection is wrong: ``` import_local_jsonl({ path: "D:\downloads\session.jsonl" }) import_local_jsonl({ path: "D:\downloads\unknown.jsonl", format: "claude" }) ``` `import_chatgpt` / `import_opencode` / `import_zcode` / `import_hermes` always return a batch result — one file / database holds all conversations, so each conversation becomes its own session in a single call.
Import parameters & behaviors - `preview: true` (alias `dryRun: true`) — run the import **read-only**: resolve, read and convert exactly like a real import, but persist nothing (zero side effects). Drop the flag and call again to actually import. - `force: true` — create a **fresh full copy** under a new id (`import--`) even when the source was already imported; the old session is never modified. - `sessionId` (optional) — override the target ChatCode CLI session id (default `import-`). - `import_chatgpt({ branch: 'all' })` — restore **every root→leaf branch** of the conversation DAG as its own session (the main thread stays the last-child chain; branch sessions carry a suffixed source id and a branch-marked title). Tool messages in the export are restored as real `tool/call` + `tool/result` (structured JSON arguments, FIFO pairing) instead of plain text. - `import_claude({ compacted: true })` — import only the **last compression summary + tail** of a long session (summary restored as a leading `reasoning` block; title from the summary record). Without a summary record the flag has no effect. - `import_hermes({ lineage: 'tail' })` — import only **leaf chain tails** (sessions that are not any other session's parent); compaction-fork parent sessions are skipped and annotated. - `import_chat({ format: 'reasonix', path: '' })` — directory imports default to `lineageMode: 'canonical'`. A recovery ancestor is collapsed only when modern sidecar metadata places both files in the same logical topic, an unambiguous `parent_id` chain proves ancestry, and its complete semantic message sequence is a proper prefix of a longer descendant. Malformed inputs, WAL-backed checkpoints, exact duplicates, missing lineage links, and divergent leaves are retained. This does not choose one active leaf from Reasonix's catalog; genuine branches remain separate. Use `lineageMode: 'physical'` for one session per JSONL. - **Archived sessions are re-importable** — ChatCode CLI's archive hides a session from the sidebar but keeps it (and its id) in persistence, so the panel and `scan_discover` report an archived target as **已归档 / Archived** with a re-import button. Importing again creates a fresh copy under a new id (`import--`, same minting as `force`) without touching the archived session; the same applies per-session inside multi-session sources (chatgpt / opencode / zcode / hermes DBs). - **Incremental re-import** — re-importing the same source never rewrites imported history. Unchanged files are skipped (`already-imported`) without re-reading; grown files append only their **new turns** to the same session (`appended`); truncated files are detected and reported (`sourceShrunk`) — use `force: true` for a complete fresh copy: ``` import_claude({ path: "C:\Users\\.claude\projects\\.jsonl" }) // unchanged → "already-imported" · grew → "appended" (new turns only) ```
Every import result reports its `status` and any anomalies — malformed lines, suspected secrets, per-source drops — nothing is silently swallowed. ### import_agents — convert pi/opencode/Claude/Codex agents, prompts, skills & config into ChatCode CLI skills `import_agents` converts custom agents, mode prompts, skills, instructions and config references from **pi** (`~/.pi/agent/{agents,prompts}/*.md`), **opencode** (`~/.config/opencode/{agents,skill}/*.md`), **Claude** (`~/.claude/memory//*.md`, `~/.claude/skills//SKILL.md`, or an explicit project-root `CLAUDE.md` via `claudeProjectRoot`) and **Codex** (`~/.codex/skills//SKILL.md`, `~/.codex/instructions.md`, `~/.codex/AGENTS.md`, `~/.codex/config.toml`) into **persistent ChatCode CLI skill assets** — `$DSH_AGENTS_HOME/skills//SKILL.md` (`$DSH_AGENTS_HOME` is a preserved plugin-ABI variable and defaults to `~/.agents`), so they become discoverable skills in any session. This complements the runtime-only Claude bridge (`context-bridge`, off by default): that one injects Claude memory/CLAUDE.md/skills transiently; this one persists them (plus pi/opencode/Codex assets). By default it **dry-runs** (returns the write/complete/skip plan with zero side effects); pass `apply: true` to actually write: ``` import_agents() // dry-run: plan only import_agents({ apply: true }) // write $DSH_AGENTS_HOME/skills//SKILL.md import_agents({ codexRoot: "~/.codex", apply: true }) // include Codex assets explicitly ``` Semantics: same-name conflicts across sources get a `-` suffix (e.g. `-pi` / `-opencode` / `-codex`); identical content is skipped (idempotent); sources already carrying `kind: dsh`/`kind: skill` frontmatter are not re-imported; a bundle directory that lacks `SKILL.md` is completed in place (preserving existing `scripts/` etc.); nested YAML (e.g. `permission:`) is preserved. Scope note: `import_agents` is a lightweight asset mover. The plugin bundle loads hooks, MCP and commands on each startup; see the [README](../README.md#hooks-mcp-and-commands). Use `import_assets` for an explicit configuration migration (preview by default, `apply: true` to write). ### scan_discover — read-only session discovery `scan_discover` scans the known data roots of all 17 formats (including the Reasonix desktop app and Claude-3p roots on Windows) and returns a structured session index (title, project, cwd, path, import status, and git branch/dirty when the source directory is a git repo) so you can preview before a batch import. Zero side effects: ``` scan_discover() scan_discover({ path: "~/.codex/sessions", format: "codex", query: "import" }) ``` ### list_imported_sessions & retract_import — identify & retract `list_imported_sessions()` enumerates every ChatCode CLI session this plugin has imported; `retract_import({ sessionId })` (or `sourcePath`) removes its registry record and returns manual-deletion guidance. **Identification and guided manual deletion only — nothing is ever deleted**: ``` list_imported_sessions() retract_import({ sessionId: "import-019f5f27-…" }) ``` > **Ghost sessions after retract (#22)** — the ChatCode CLI host has no delete/forget API: after `retract_import` and manual artifact deletion, the session id may still occupy the host's in-memory index (it stays visible until `chatcode-cli` restarts, and re-importing the same source used to fail with `session "…" already exists in this backend`). Re-import now detects the stale entry and **automatically mints a suffixed new session id** (`import--1`) with a clear `staleGhost: { previous, current }` report; the manual-deletion guidance also notes that a restart is needed to clear the ghost. ### export_chat — ChatCode CLI → Claude / Codex / Kimi (matrix export) `export_chat({ format: "claude", sessionId })` serializes an existing ChatCode CLI session (imported or native) into a Claude Code JSONL transcript, ready for `--resume`. It is written to `//.jsonl` (default `~/.claude/projects`), with a fresh UUID v4 file name — an existing file is never overwritten. `format: "codex"` and `format: "kimi"` write Codex rollout JSONL and Kimi `wire.jsonl` respectively (default `~/.chatcode-cli/exports`, or `path: …` to pick a target), completing the ChatCode CLI↔Claude↔Codex↔Kimi matrix. Every export lists its **lossy items** in a `degradations` field — nothing is silently dropped: ``` export_chat({ format: "claude", sessionId: "import-019f5f27-…" }) export_chat({ format: "codex", sessionId: "…", dryRun: true }) export_chat({ format: "kimi", sessionId: "…", outputDir: "D:\backup\kimi" }) ``` ### export_bundle / restore_bundle — portable interchange bundle `export_bundle({ sessionId })` writes a **`.dshbundle.json`** — an event-level lossless interchange bundle (protocol: [docs/INTERCHANGE.md](docs/INTERCHANGE.md)) with double SHA-256 fingerprints (session-level + file-level) and machine-independent landing info (`originalCwd` + `landingHint`). `restore_bundle({ path })` verifies the fingerprints (corruption is reported loudly, never restored silently), then imports the session through the same idempotent state machine — repeat restores skip, `force: true` makes a copy, directory mode restores every `.dshbundle.json`: ``` export_bundle({ sessionId: "import-019f5f27-…" }) // → ~/.chatcode-cli/exports/.dshbundle.json restore_bundle({ path: "D:\backup\sess.dshbundle.json" }) // machine A → machine B restore_bundle({ path: "D:\backup\bundle-dir", preview: true }) // dry-run ``` **Cross-machine (REQ-62):** export on machine A, copy the bundle, restore on machine B. When the original `cwd` does not exist there, the session falls back to the bundle file's directory (REQ-39-lite grouping) and the result reports `cwdAvailable: false` / `groupedTo` / `restoreNote` — never silent. ### verify_session — read-only structural audit `verify_session({ sessionId })` runs a read-only structural check on any ChatCode CLI session: seq continuity, event-type whitelist, `surfaceOp` on surface events, `sourceEventSeqs` pointing at real `tool/call`s, turn/step balance, and tool-call↔result pairing. Problems are located one-by-one, and per-kind `repairHints` tell you what to do: ``` verify_session({ sessionId: "import-019f5f27-…" }) ``` ### doctor — read-only migration health check `doctor()` runs a read-only health check after migration: imports registry readability, whether every imported session still exists in `sessionPersistence`, whether `import_agents` skills were persisted, and whether `workspaceRegistry` is available. It never writes, imports, syncs, or deletes anything: ``` doctor() ``` It returns `{ ok, checks, issues, totals }` — useful after a large batch import or before/after moving ChatCode CLI data between machines. ### standalone CLI — export-md / doctor The npm package also ships a small standalone CLI (no ChatCode CLI host required): ``` npx --package @chatcode/cco-chat-import cco-chat-import export-md ~/.chatcode-cli/sessions///session.jsonl npx --package @chatcode/cco-chat-import cco-chat-import export-md --out session.md npx --package @chatcode/cco-chat-import cco-chat-import doctor ``` `export-md` renders a ChatCode CLI session log as readable Markdown. `doctor` reads `$CHATCODE_CLI_HOME/cco-chat-import/imports.json` (falling back to legacy `$DSH_HOME` only when the new variable is absent) and the local `sessions` tree for a lightweight health summary. ### import_mcp — MCP mirror plan `import_mcp` reads MCP servers from **Claude** (`~/.claude.json` / `.mcp.json`) and **Codex** (`~/.codex/config.toml`) and generates a reviewable **ChatCode CLI MCP client YAML snippet**. By default it dry-runs; `apply: true` writes the snippet to `$CHATCODE_CLI_HOME/cco-chat-import/mcp-mirror.cordis.yml` (or `outPath`) — it never edits your profile automatically: ``` import_mcp() // dry-run: list servers + YAML snippet import_mcp({ apply: true }) // write generated snippet /mcp-status // list discovered servers ``` ### import_settings — settings/config translation suggestions `import_settings` reads **Claude `~/.claude/settings.json`** and **Codex `~/.codex/config.toml`** and returns migration suggestions for ChatCode CLI: model binding, permission rules, hooks, environment variables, and model provider. It is read-only and never applies anything: ``` import_settings() // list suggestions /settings-suggest // same via slash command ``` ### sync_to_claude — incremental write-back `sync_to_claude({ sessionId })` appends a session's **new complete turns** back to its Claude Code file — `target: "source"` by default (the import source) or `"copy"` (the last `export_chat` `format: "claude"` copy). Guards report an externally modified or shrunken file instead of overwriting it; `force: true` re-anchors past external edits (the overridden guard is still reported): ``` sync_to_claude({ sessionId: "import-019f5f27-…" }) sync_to_claude({ sessionId: "…", target: "copy", dryRun: true }) ``` ### Browser panel — discover & import from the sidebar The `chatcode-cli web` sidebar shows an **导入会话** button in its footer. It opens a panel listing discovered sessions **grouped by workspace folder**, with source and status filters, search, pagination, and bulk import. The panel closes on `Escape`. Each row supports **single import**, and the checkboxes enable **multi-select import** ("导入所选 (N)"): the panel calls the same host import pipeline as the `import_*` tools, so idempotent skip / incremental append / `force` / context-budget semantics are identical, and the list refreshes with the new statuses after importing. A multi-session source (e.g. `conversations.json`, an opencode/zcode/hermes DB) is imported whole — opencode/zcode restrict to the selected `sessionId`s. > The data comes from the same read-only discovery as `scan_discover` (30s TTL cache + persistent mtime bookmarks); the panel itself never writes anything except the imports you trigger. ### `/import` slash command & `/resume-*` handoff The plugin also registers a **`/import `** slash command (available where the compatibility `commands` service is mounted): type it directly in a session to import without a model round-trip — the same pipeline and semantics as the `import_*` tools. **`/import-all [source] [path]`** scans the default data roots (or one source / explicit path) and imports every not-yet-imported session in one shot — same pipeline, idempotent skip / incremental append, archived sessions skipped, failures reported individually. **`/attach-workspaces`** re-attaches already-imported sessions to their cwd-matched workspaces from the imports registry — useful for fixing early imports that landed in “未分组” or whose workspace attach previously failed. It is idempotent and safe to re-run. Options: `--mode auto|dedicated|per-project` and `--dir ` (for `dedicated`). **`/doctor`** runs the same read-only health check as the `doctor` tool and prints a concise report. **`/mcp-status`** scans both user and current-session project MCP configuration, showing server names and source paths; project names take precedence. **`/hooks`** reports user settings, project settings and settings.local hooks; **`/agents`** lists user and project agents. Configuration discovery does not prove execution; restart the CLI after changes. **`/settings-suggest`** lists Claude/Codex config translation suggestions (read-only); use `import_settings` for the structured tool output. **`/import-reset`** clears the scan cache (in-memory TTL + persistent `scan-cache.json`) when discovery results look stale; imported sessions are untouched. **`/resume-claude [id: | keyword]`** and **`/resume-codex`** generate a **handoff summary** from an external transcript and inject it into the current session so you can continue the work in ChatCode CLI, treating the transcript as untrusted static history. ``` /resume-claude id:282095ab-1111-4222-8333-444455556666 /resume-codex 修复登录 ``` ### Session-start context enhancements Two optional hooks run when a ChatCode CLI session starts (the preserved host `agent/session-start` event), both agent-scoped and never touching your transcripts: - **Migration hint (default on)** — set `CHATCODE_CLI_IMPORT_SESSION_HINT=0` to disable. Legacy `DSH_IMPORT_SESSION_HINT` is read only when the new variable is absent. - **Claude context bridge (default off)** — set `CHATCODE_CLI_IMPORT_CONTEXT_BRIDGE=1` to bridge Claude Code context assets into the session. Legacy `DSH_IMPORT_CONTEXT_BRIDGE` remains a lower-priority compatibility input.

# 使用详解 > 从 README 迁出的完整工具/命令用法。快速上手见 README「使用」一节。 ## 🛠 使用 `/import cco <路径>` 支持 Web ZIP、TUI JSONL 及原生日志目录。Web ZIP 直接导入，无需手动解压；主会话及子会话独立创建，附件缺失或损坏时明确报错。`import_chat({ format: "cco", path, preview: true })` 只预览，不创建会话或保存附件。旧 `dsh` 参数保留兼容。 TUI 会话可用 `/export`（或 `/export jsonl`）导出原生 JSONL 日志，再用 `/import cco <导出文件的绝对路径>` 导入，通过 `/resume` 打开导入会话。目录导入也会收集 TUI JSONL 导出和 `session.vN.jsonl` 日志。导入器补齐格式及分支元数据，创建独立的根会话。`/export markdown` 用于阅读，`.md` 不能作为原生日志导入。JSONL 不打包附件文件和子会话。 > **首次迁移分步流程**（以下步骤用于会话历史；启动时加载 hooks、MCP 和 commands 的行为见 [README](../README.zh-CN.md)）： > ① **预览** - `scan_discover()` 或侧边栏面板查看可导入会话与导入状态徽标；或任一 `import_*` 传 `preview: true` 零副作用试跑。 > ② **导入** - 去掉 `preview` 正式导入，按来源 / 工作区核对逐会话 `status`（重复导入行为见下文「增量续写」）。 > ③ **体检与撤回** - `doctor()` 只读体检；`retract_import` 撤回 registry 记录，或面板「历史」页删除本插件创建的会话（需确认）。 > **注意**：导入会即时落盘，但 ChatCode CLI 的会话列表不会自动刷新——导入后请刷新页面（或会话列表）才能看到新会话。 **导入——单个文件或目录。** 每个 `import_*` 工具都接受 `path`；目录递归扫描，每个文件 / 每段对话成为独立会话： ``` import_claude({ path: "C:\Users\\.claude\projects\\.jsonl" }) import_codex({ path: "C:\Users\\.codex\sessions\2026\05\18\rollout-2026-05-18T21-14-16-xxxx.jsonl" }) import_chatgpt({ path: "C:\Users\\Downloads\chatgpt-export\conversations.json" }) import_opencode({ path: "C:\Users\\.local\share\opencode\opencode.db" }) import_local_jsonl({ path: "D:\downloads\session.jsonl" }) ``` `import_local_jsonl({ path })` 接受任意本地 `.jsonl` 会话文件（或目录）：自动识别 `dsh` / `claude` / `codex` / `cursor` / `reasonix` / `pi` / `openclaw` / `hermes`，识别不准时可用 `format` 参数强制指定： ``` import_local_jsonl({ path: "D:\downloads\session.jsonl" }) import_local_jsonl({ path: "D:\downloads\unknown.jsonl", format: "claude" }) ``` `import_chatgpt` / `import_opencode` / `import_zcode` / `import_hermes` 恒返回批量结果——一个文件 / 数据库包含全部会话，一次调用即可让每段对话成为独立会话。
导入参数与行为 - `preview: true`（别名 `dryRun: true`）— **只读**运行：照常解析 / 读取 / 转换，但**零副作用**、不落盘。去掉该参数再调一次即正式导入。 - `force: true` — 即使已导入，也以新 id（`import--`）另存一份**完整副本**；旧会话绝不修改。 - `sessionId`（可选）— 覆盖目标 ChatCode CLI 会话 id（默认 `import-<源sessionId>`）。 - `import_chatgpt({ branch: 'all' })` — 把对话 DAG 的**每条 root→leaf 分支**还原为独立会话（主线程仍是最后 child 链；分支会话带后缀源 id 与分支标记标题）。导出里的工具消息还原为真正的 `tool/call` + `tool/result`（结构化 JSON 参数、FIFO 配对），不再是纯文本。 - `import_claude({ compacted: true })` — 只导长会话的**最后一次压缩摘要 + 尾部**（摘要作前置 `reasoning` 块；标题取 summary 记录）。无 summary 记录时该参数不生效。 - `import_hermes({ lineage: 'tail' })` — 只导**叶子链尾**（不是任何其它会话父会话的会话）；压缩分叉父会话跳过并标注。 - `import_chat({ format: 'reasonix', path: '' })` — 目录导入默认使用 `lineageMode: 'canonical'`。只有现代 sidecar 把两个文件归入同一逻辑话题、无歧义的 `parent_id` 链明确证明祖先关系，而且祖先的完整语义消息序列是更长后代的真前缀时，才折叠恢复祖先。畸形输入、带 WAL 的检查点、完全相同副本、谱系链缺失及真实分叉叶全部保留。此模式不会替 Reasonix catalog 选择唯一活动叶；真实分支继续独立存在。`lineageMode: 'physical'` 可恢复每个 JSONL 一条会话。 - **已归档会话可重新导入** — ChatCode CLI 的归档会把会话从侧边栏隐藏，但保留在持久化里（及其 id）。再次导入以新 id（`import--`，与 `force` 同一铸键）另存完整副本，不触碰已归档会话。 - **增量续写（重导）** — 重导同一源路径绝不改写已导入历史：未变文件跳过（`already-imported`，不重读）；增长文件只把**新增轮次** append 进同一会话（`appended`）；截断文件检测并上报（`sourceShrunk`）——需要完整新副本时用 `force: true`： ``` import_claude({ path: "C:\Users\\.claude\projects\\.jsonl" }) // 未变化 → "already-imported" · 增长 → "appended"（只追加新轮次） ```
每次导入结果都会上报 `status` 与任何异常——畸形行、疑似敏感信息、逐源丢弃——绝不静默吞掉。 ### import_agents — 把 pi/opencode/Claude/Codex 的 agent、prompt、skill、指令与配置参考转换为 ChatCode CLI skills `import_agents` 把 **pi**、**opencode**、**Claude** 与 **Codex** 的自定义 agent、prompt、skill、指令与配置参考转换为**持久化 ChatCode CLI skill 资产**——`$DSH_AGENTS_HOME/skills//SKILL.md`。`DSH_AGENTS_HOME` 是保留的插件 ABI 变量，缺省为 `~/.agents`。 默认 **dry-run**（只返回 write/complete/skip 规划清单，零副作用）；传 `apply: true` 才真正写盘： ``` import_agents() // dry-run：仅规划 import_agents({ apply: true }) // 写入 $DSH_AGENTS_HOME/skills//SKILL.md import_agents({ codexRoot: "~/.codex", apply: true }) // 显式包含 Codex 资产 ``` 语义：跨源同名冲突加 `-` 后缀消歧（如 `-pi` / `-opencode` / `-codex`）；内容相同幂等跳过；已带 `kind: dsh`/`kind: skill` frontmatter 的源不重复导入；bundle 目录缺 `SKILL.md` 时原地补全（保留既有 `scripts/` 等）；嵌套 YAML（如
